newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly slide again, demand weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly slide again, demand weak.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly moved lower again Wednesday, with trade still quiet but sentiment more bearish amid slack utility demand and prospects for better avails, industry sources said.
"The numbers (prices) are leaning weaker. There's still no demand and more barrels coming in," said one cash trader, noting the potential next month for several high and low sulphur cargoes.
In New York Harbor, high sulphurs continued to lose ground, with 2.2 percent down a quarter to about $19.50-75 a barrel and three percent off the same at about $19.
NYH physical one percent slipped 25 cents to about $21, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent also lost a quarter to $18.50-75, while three percent eased slightly to $18.00-25, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
November New York City gate gas prices slid a few cents Wednesday to the high-$3.20s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.33/mmBtu equivalent.
